body.heading: Small enough to start today
paragraphs: A hundred dollars is a deliberately humble target. At $5 a week it takes twenty weeks; at $10 a week, ten weeks. The amount matters less than the finish line being close enough to see from where you stand.
Choose a weekly figure you could manage even in a bad week. A plan that survives bad weeks is worth ten ambitious plans that collapse by the second one.

body.heading: Make it visible and separate
paragraphs: Keep the hundred in its own pot or account, with a name if your bank allows it — "First 100" works fine. Watching the number climb is the reward that carries you through the weeks when motivation dips.
Separate matters for another reason too: money mixed into everyday spending gets spent. A named pot has a job, and most of us hesitate before raiding a pot with a purpose.

body.heading: When you get there
paragraphs: Leave the hundred where it is. It has quietly become your starter emergency cushion — the thing that turns a broken phone screen from a crisis into an inconvenience. Then set the next target, perhaps $250, using exactly the habit you have just built.
Tell someone, too. A hundred saved is a small, real achievement, and saying it aloud makes it harder to quietly undo on a dull evening. Habits grow stronger when they are witnessed kindly.

takeaway: Save your first $100 in a separate, named pot at a pace that survives bad weeks — the habit you build is worth more than the amount.
